To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the downregulation of PKCδ contributes to the reduced α-adrenoceptor mediated signaling cascade in the aortes of obese mice.

(1) IP3 receptor and PKC are involved in α1-adrenoceptors signaling pathway in mouse aortae; (2) the reduced expression and function of IP3 receptor contribute to the reduced contraction of aortae from obese mice; (3) the down-regulated PKCδ contributes to the reduced contraction.

in aortae from high fat diet-fed obese mice, phenylephine-induced contraction was reduced due to the down-regulated IP3 receptor expression and phosphorylation and the down-regulation of PKCδ expression and phosphorylation, which may contribute to the development of obesity-related cardiovascular complications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of IP3 and PKC in the down-regulated α1-adrenoceptors signaling in aortae from DIO mice.
the role of IP3/PKCδ signaling cascade in the down-regulation of vascular α1-adrenoceptors in obesity.
the down-regulation of PKCδ and PKCζ but not PKCβ in DIO mouse vasculature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the down-regulated PKCδ contributes to the reduction of α-adrenoceptors-mediated contraction in the mouse aortae of obese mice, which is likely due to the decreased expression and phosphorylation levels of IP3 receptor.
PKCδ is the key isoform that maintains the α1-adrenoceptors-mediated contraction of aortic smooth muscle in obesity.
the reduced expression and activity of PKCδ, rather than IP3 receptor, contribute to the down-regulation of phenylephrine-activated signaling cascade in aortae from DIO mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PKCδ contributes to the down-regulated α1-adrenoceptors-mediated signaling cascade and thus attenuates phenylephrine-contractile responses in aortae from DIO mice.

the reduced expression of IP3 receptor, PKCδ and PKCζ and their phosphorylations contribute to the down-regulation of phenylephrine-contracted aortae in DIO mice, and PKCδ may play a more important role in this process.
obesity reduces α1-adrenoceptors and IP3 receptor-mediated Ca2+ release, and PKCδ contributes to maintain phenylepherine-mediated contraction in aortas of DIO mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PKCδ contributes to the reduction of phenylephrine-contracted force in the aortas of DIO mice.
PKCδ plays a critical role in α1-adrenoceptors signaling in obesity.
PKCδ is more likely to maintain α-adrenoceptor agonists-induced contraction in the aorta of obese mice.
